question: What is the chemical formula of sodium nitrate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**NaNO3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sodium nitrate is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula **NaNO3**.
 
• It is a white, crystalline solid that is highly soluble in water.
 
• Sodium nitrate is commonly used in fertilizers, food preservatives, and in the production of explosives.
 
• It is also known as Chile saltpeter due to its large deposits found in Chile.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inorganic Compounds:**

 
 
• These compounds generally do not contain carbon-hydrogen bonds.
 
• They are typically minerals and include salts, metals, and other elemental compounds.
 
 
 
• **Solubility:**
 
 
• The ability of a substance to dissolve in a solvent, such as water.
 
• Sodium nitrate is highly soluble in water, making it useful in various applications.
 
 
 
• **Fertilizers:**
 
 
• Substances that provide essential nutrients to plants to promote growth.
 
• Sodium nitrate supplies nitrogen, which is a crucial nutrient for plant growth.
 
 
 
• **Food Preservatives:**
 
 
• Substances added to food to prevent spoilage and extend shelf life.
 
• Sodium nitrate is used to preserve meats and prevent the growth of harmful bacteria.
